buyer_added_terms.text: 1. Generic OPTION CLAUSE 25% : The buyer can increase or decrease the contract quantity or contract duration up to 25 percent at the time of issue of the contract. However, once the contract is issued, the contract quantity or contract duration can only be increased up to 25 percent. Bidders are bound to accept the revised quantity or duration. For lumpsum-based service contracts, the buyer may increase the scope of work and contract value up to 25 percent with the consent of the service provider

2. Generic Bidder financial standing: The bidder should not be under liquidation, court receivership or similar proceedings, should not be bankrupt. Bidder to upload undertaking to this effect with bid. 3. Generic Actual delivery (and Installation & Commissioning (if covered in scope of supply)) is to be done at following address The Commandant Naval War College C/o INS Mandovi Verem Goa - 403109 . 4. Generic Registration / Empanelment Requirement: Contract shall be awarded to only such sellers , who are registered / empanelled / approved / enlisted with Government for the required goods / service category on the date of bid opening. Prospective bidders (if not already registered), are advised to get themselves registered with the said registration authority before bid opening date. (It is certified that the registration is granted by the registering agency as per Rule 150 of GFR following a fair, transparent and reasonable procedure.) 5. Service & Support AVAILABILITY OF OFFICE OF SERVICE PROVIDER: An office of the Service Provider must be located in the state of Consignee. DOCUMENTARY EVIDENCE TO BE SUBMITTED. 6. Service & Support Dedicated /toll Free Telephone No. for Service Support : BIDDER/OEM must have Dedicated/toll Free Telephone No. for Service Support. 7. Service & Support Escalation Matrix For Service Support : Bidder/OEM must provide Escalation Matrix of Telephone Numbers for Service Support. 8. Certificates Bidder's offer is liable to be rejected if they don't upload any of the certificates / documents sought in the Bid document, ATC and Corrigendum if any. 9. Payment PAYMENT OF SALARIES AND WAGES: Service Provider is required to pay Salaries / wages of contracted staff deployed at buyer location first i.e. on their own and then claim payment from Buyer alongwith all statutory documents like, PF, ESIC etc. as well as the bank statement of payment done to staff. 10. Past Project Experience Proof for Past Experience and Project Experience clause: For fulfilling the experience criteria any one of the following documents may be considered as valid proof for meeting the experience criteria:a. Contract copy along with Invoice(s) with self-certification by the bidder that service/supplies against the invoices have been executed.b. Execution certificate by client with contract value.c. Any other document in support of contract execution like Third Party Inspection release note, etc.Proof for Past Experience and Project Experience clause: For fulfilling the experience criteria any one of the following documents may be

considered as valid proof for meeting the experience criteria:a. Contract copy along with Invoice(s) with self-certification by the bidder that service/supplies against the invoices have been executed.b. Execution certificate by client with contract value.c. Any other document in support of contract execution like Third Party Inspection release note, etc. 11. Forms of EMD and PBG Bidders can also submit the EMD with Account Payee Demand Draft in favour of The Commandant, Naval War College payable at PCDA (N) Mumbai . Bidder has to upload scanned copy / proof of the DD along with bid and has to ensure delivery of hardcopy to the Buyer within 5 days of Bid End date / Bid Opening date. 12. Forms of EMD and PBG Successful Bidder can submit the Performance Security in the form of Account Payee Demand Draft also (besides PBG which is allowed as per GeM GTC). DD should be made in favour of The Commandant, Naval War College payable at PCDA (N) Mumbai . After award of contract, Successful Bidder can upload scanned copy of the DD in place of PBG and has to ensure delivery of hard copy to the original DD to the Buyer within 15 days of award of contract. 13. Buyer Added Bid Specific ATC Buyer Added text based ATC clauses 1. The seller should preferably have a registered office in the state of buyer location and documents for ad dress proof to be submitted with the bid. However, in case if the bidder is selected as L1 firm, it has to ope n a working office in the locality of the bidder. It is further submitted that this condition is not restrictive an d solely been included for better administration of the manpower related matters. 2. Minimum service charge is not below than 3.85% as per latest GoI directives. A self declaration certificat e must be attached for quoting not below 3.85%. 3. Bid security declaration be submitted instead of EMD as per GOI/MOE letter no F.9/4/2020-PPD dated 12 Nov 20. 4.Acceptance of ATC- A self declaration to be made by the bidder at the time bidding quoting acceptance of all terms and condition and ATC mentioned in the bid documents on its letter head duly signed by the c oncerned authority. 5.Bidder shall submit the following documents along with their bid for Vendor Code Creation: a.Copy of PAN Card. b. Copy of GSTIN. c. Copy of Cancelled Cheque. d. Copy of EFT Mandate duly certified by Bank. 6. NON DISCLOSURE DECLARATION CERTIFICATE (On Bidder Letter Head) to be uploaded with bid: I M/s.(Bi dder Name/ staff name) hereby declare that I shall not disclose the contract or any provision,specification, plan, design, pattern, sample or information thereof to any third party during and after expiry of Contract a nd the successful bidder has to ensure that all the staff deployed at buyer location should also furnish the same declaration. If defying the norms as per the Contract a legal action may be taken against me as per the existing Rules. 7. An interview will be undertaken by the BOO after award of the bid for selection of the staffs and the succ

essful bidder must provide joining letter, monthly salary slip and experience certificate to all the staff depl oyed at buyer location during and after conclusion of the contract respectively. A declaration for the same must provided by the bidder at the time of bidding. 8. The Industrial Relations Code (IR Code), 2020: 8.1. Contractor providing services of contracted employees cannot terminate their services abruptly witho ut a prior notice of 14 days. 8.2. Grievance Redressal Committee (GRC): A Grievance Redressal Committee (GRC) is to be established, i f a unit establishment has 20 or more employees (including outsourced workers) for resolution of wor kplace grievances. All outsourced workers are to be provided with the access to GRC. 8.3. Standing Orders (applicable for department with strength of workers in excess of 300). Model Standin g Orders must be promulgated for Organisations/establishments with 300 or more workers. Contractor must abide by the departments' standing orders regarding discipline, conduct, working hours, termination, etc. 9. The Code of Social Security, 2020: 9.1. EPF (Employees' Provident Fund) (applicable when contractor employs 20 or more workers). Contracto r must register workers under EPF and a monthly deposit of relevant share (12% to be contributed by employer and 12% by the employee) must be credited. A monthly ECR (Electronic Challan-cum-Return) wit h respect to such deposits must be retained by the contractor. Principal Employer must verify that PF is be ing deposited and obtain PF compliance certificate every month. 9.2 ESI (Employees' State Insurance) (applicable when monthly wages of the employees are below Rs.21,0 00/-). Contractor must register eligible workers under ESIC and contributions must be deposited on a mont hly basis. They are also to ensure medical, sickness and disablement benefits. Principal Employer must ver ify ESI compliance and maintain ESI details of each worker. 9.3. Maternity Benefit Act (for female outsourced workers). Contractor must provide paid maternity leave as per the law and Principal Employer must ensure no discrimination in employment conditions. 9.4. Employees' Compensation (if ESI not applicable). If a worker is not covered under ESI, then the contra ctor must provide compensation for injury, disability or death on duty, as applicable. Principal Employer must ensure insurance coverage for the employees through the contractor. 9.5 "The contractor shall comply with the code on Wages, Industrial Relations Code, Social Security Code a nd Occupational Safety, Health & Working Conditions Code. Wages shall be paid as per the revised definiti on of 'Wages'. PF/ ESI challan, wage transfer proof, attendance records and statutory registers shall be sub mitted monthly before invoice acceptance." 9.6 Strike/ Lockout Notice Clause: "The contractor shall ensure continuity of services and comply with the provisions of the Industrial Relation Code, 2020 related to strike/ lockout. Any disruption without statutory notice shall be treated as breach of contract". 9.7 GRC Clause: "All employees shall have access to the establishment's Grievance Redressal Committee. The contractor shall cooperate with the GRC as required." 9.8 Standing Orders Compliance: "Deployed personnel shall adhere to the Standing Orders of the establish ment as per the IR Code, 2020."

9.9 EPF Compliance: "Contractor shall ensure EPF coverage for all deployed employees as per the Code on Social Security, 2020. Monthly ECR and payment receipt shall be submitted to the Principal Employer". 9.10 ESI Compliance: "Contractor shall provide ESI benefit as per Social Security Code, 2020 and submit m onthly contribution challans". 9.11 Accident/ Insurance Clause: "In case a worker is not covered under ESI contractor shall ensure covera ge under Employees' Compensation insurance". 9.12 OSH Compliance Clause: "The contractor shall comply with Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020 during execution of the contract". 9.13 Working Hours Clause: "Working hours shall follow OSH Code norms. 8 hours/day, 48hours/week;over time shall be paid at double rate". 10. Wage-Related Compliance (As per The Code of Wages, 2019): 10.1. As per the new definition of "Wages", Basic Pay + DA must work out to minimum 50% of total wages. 10.2. Emoluments like PF, ESI, Bonus, Leave, Gratuity must be calculated on the wages as defined above. 10.3. Minimum Wages notified by Government of India must be compulsorily adhered to. 10.4. Units shall hold separate files for maintaining records of contract labour compliance, monthly statuto ry compliance checklist, digital copies of all PF/ESI challans, contract license details, wage registers & attendance. 11. The Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions (OSH) Code, 2020: 11.1. Safety and Health Measures at Workplace: Units must ensure safe working environment, PPE & unifor ms (where applicable), drinking water, sanitation, first-aid box and rest arrangements. Mandatory free ann ual health check-ups for contracted employees are to be provided by the employers. 11.2. Occupational Health, Medical Check-Ups: The contractor must conduct periodic medical check-ups a nd maintain health records for security personnel, cleaning staff and those employed in roles of dang erous industrial jobs. OSHA-compliance penalty is to be applied, if ignored. 11.3. Working Hours & Overtime: Daily working hours for outsourced employees should be restricted to a maximum of eight hours with a weekly limit of 48 hours. Overtime workers are to be paid double wage s as per the OSH Code. Women can work at night, only with consent and safety arrangements. 12. Bidder should submit GST registration Number & SAC code of the pertinent services. 13.Retention of sourcing power an Non-levy of sourcing fees: - The successful bidder shall mandatorily abs orb/retain at least 80% of the existing experienced operational personnel currently deployed at the Buyer's premises, subject to their satisfactory performance, background verification, and medical fit ness. the incoming contractor shall issue fresh deployment/ engagement letters to such retained staff with in 7 days of contract award without charging any registration, recruitment, administrative or onboarding fe e directly or indirectly from the personnel. failure to retain the mandated percentage without explicit writt en permission from the buyer shall constitute a breach of contract. . 14. Service & Support

The Service Provider is required to have at least 40 % of the required manpower on service provider’s payroll for at least one year. Necessary documents relating to such manpower will be uploaded by the bidder for verification of the buyer. Such manpower will be part of total manpower to be provided by the Service Provider in case he gets the contract against this bid.
